notable_absence.finding: The Serverless Environments paragraph ('Recent SDKs offer better resilience in handling errors that may occur when running your application in serverless environments... official support for AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, and GCP Functions') is a real capability-availability claim but names no SDK version and no Server version - 'recent SDKs' is not quotable as a version threshold. Rather than fabricate a version, this was left uncaptured. The same applies to the OS-compatibility lists (specific Linux distro/version support) - true facts, but enumerable platform support rather than a version-gated capability, and modeling each distro as its own concept would produce ~15 low-value single-relation concepts for one page.

cross_component_finding: quarkus:extension's dependency on version:sdk-3-7-7 inverts the direction every other availableSince relation on this page takes: elsewhere, a Server or SDK version is the threshold that gates a capability the SDK exposes; here, a downstream integration built ON TOP of the SDK (Quarkus) sets its own minimum-SDK-version requirement. Both are legitimately availableSince, but the 'who depends on whom' arrow points opposite ways, and reconciliation should not assume every availableSince edge on version:sdk-* objects flows from Server-capability-availability.
cross_product_finding: This page surfaces at least three independent version axes in play simultaneously for one product: (1) version:server-* (Couchbase Server's own release number, e.g. 7.6, 8.0), (2) version:sdk-* (the Java SDK's own release number, e.g. 3.9.0, 3.12), and (3) version:sdk-api-* (the abstract, cross-language 'SDK API specification' version, e.g. 3.9, shared by all Couchbase SDKs but incremented on its own schedule - Java 3.9 & 3.10 both implement API 3.8, while Java 3.11 & 3.12 implement API 3.9). The page explicitly warns that axes (2) and (3) only coincidentally share digits for some SDKs ('these two numbers match for the .NET SDK, this is not the case for the others'), which is captured here via shouldNotBeConfusedWith rather than conflating version:sdk-3-9-0 (a real Java release) with version:sdk-api-3-9 (the abstract spec number). A fourth, even more independent axis appears in the Spring Data Couchbase table (SDC 5.4-5.5 / SDC 6.0), a third-party framework's own version line layered on top of both the Java SDK version and the Server version it targets - not modeled with its own version:* family here since only one SDC line boundary is evidenced on this page, but reconciliation should be aware a fourth axis exists if more SDC-versioned facts turn up elsewhere in the corpus.
